review: 2026-09 self-review — a whole-product review pass over the B-16-complete tool; the tool graded by its own discipline
method: Three high-effort subsystem reviewers (analysis/emitter, runner/CLI/reporting, cross-cutting contracts) over 30k LOC. Every candidate finding was then verified by an adversarial pass that tried to refute it; the same nine (eight findings + one design tension) survived two independent verification passes, and the three highest-impact were spot-checked in code before being written up. The round's ethic is the project's own: every fix ships with a test that REDDENS when the fix is reverted (mutation probe, per docs/reviews/b12-b15-handoff.md). The P0 runtime fix additionally carries an executed proof — the four fetch scenarios of an emitted spec run under real vitest, green with the fix, all four red without, failing with the exact error the finding describes.

severityAnchors.P0: emitted suite broken, silently passes, or lies; or the tool corrupts user files
severityAnchors.P1: wrong analysis output, docs claim contradicted by code, or a CI gap that lets P0s ship
severityAnchors.P2: performance, DX, error-message quality, design friction
severityAnchors.P3: opportunity aligned with the product's spirit

findings.title: The fetch-spec's trigger throws instead of guarding, for every getAllBy* selector shape
findings.claim: firstClickTrigger rewrote only getBy* → queryBy* (a `.replace(".getBy", ".queryBy")` that converts the getByTestId form and nothing else), so the getAllBy* forms — aria-label, role, text: the common ones, and the reason emitVitestSelector emits getAllBy — slipped through untouched. The emitted `const trigger = screen.getAllBy…()[0]` throws synchronously when the element is absent, defeating the `if (trigger)` guard below it and failing all four fetch scenarios on a correct component. Reproduced by execution: a launcher rendered inside `.map()` (harvested by the analysis, absent at mount because the array starts empty) — the spec with the old line fails all four scenarios with 'Unable to find a label'; the same spec with the fixed line passes all four.
findings.spirit: The guard exists precisely because a launcher may be absent; a guard that throws before it runs is not a guard, and a fetch spec that fails on the component it was generated for is the tool's cardinal sin in its own output.
findings.foundBy: subsystem reviewer (analysis/emitter); adversarial pass; spot-checked in code
findings.fix: The rewrite is anchored per shape: getAllBy* → queryAllBy* (an empty result's [0] is undefined), getBy* → queryBy*, querySelector keeps its assertion dropped. tests/templatesUnit.test.ts emits an aria-label launcher and pins the queryAllByLabelText trigger line — red before, green after. Executed proof: the four fetch scenarios of the emitted spec run under real vitest — pass with the new form, fail all four with the old.

findings.title: React Native's editable → disabled polarity is inverted
findings.claim: collectHints read `editable`'s truthiness as if the attribute were `disabled`: editable={true} (a working field) was marked "conditional" disabled — a dishonest skip on a live control — while editable={false} (locked) was left looking fillable. The branch inverted `disabledAtInitialRender`'s result; only the undecidable editable={expr} → "conditional" case was right, the two decidable cases were backwards. The value is dead in emitted output today (no native consumer reads hints.disabled — the DOM-only decidePostDispatch path, and the native emitter, which never calls it), but it is a real bug at the analyse() surface, where a custom reporter reads exactly this field; postDispatch.ts names this field the one DOM and native 'have drifted before'.
findings.spirit: An analyser field that says "conditionally disabled" about a working field and "fillable" about a locked one is a lie waiting for a consumer — and this field is the documented drift hazard between the two emitters.
findings.foundBy: subsystem reviewer (analysis/emitter); adversarial pass; spot-checked in code
findings.note: Landed after the useRef env fix (FR-057): a ref-gated editable now evaluates the ref as truthy, which this branch reads as "editable" — the correct reading. The ordering matters and is recorded so it is not "simplified" back.
findings.fix: A non-editable field is disabled "always", an editable one is not disabled at all, an undecidable editable stays "conditional". tests/nativeTemplates.test.ts — Locked/Open/Default/Dynamic TextInputs assert their hints.disabled at the analyse() surface; Locked and Open both redden without the fix.

findings.title: Same-named components collapse each other's inline summaries
findings.claim: writeInlineSummaries deduped components on the bare name, so a/Header.tsx and b/Header.tsx collapsed into one map entry: the second file never got its .flawless.json sidecar and every finding routed to it was silently dropped from the report — the exact sibling drop registry.ts dedupes on the full key to prevent. Reproduced: a fixture with two same-named components writes one sidecar where two are owed, and the dropped component's findings appear in no report.
findings.spirit: A report that silently routes findings into nothing is a report that lies about its own completeness — and the dedupe convention already exists one file over, unapplied.
findings.fix: collectComponents/findOwner/the write loop now key on filePath::componentName (the registry.ts convention); the sidecar keeps its bare-name filename beside each source file. tests/inlineSummaries.test.ts (new) — two Headers in a/ and b/ write both sidecars, each carrying only its own finding; a child rendered by two parents still collapses to one. Red before, green after.

findings.title: --changed exited 0 green for a change no selected spec can see
findings.claim: planAffectedRuns early-returned on empty components+routes before the file-keyed unit branch, so a change confined to an unexported component (no spec name of its own) ran no specs yet exited 0 with "changed: nothing affected" — a vacuous pass under the flag built to catch exactly that: the file changed, is covered through a parent's spec, and the run said nothing. The same empty plan mislabelled its reason whenever a name-grep-only task set (e.g. --tasks perf-harness) met an unexported-only change: "nothing affected" where the true sentence is "affected, but these tasks narrow by spec name and cannot reach it".
findings.spirit: A CI gate that says "nothing affected" about a change it knows about is the CI gap that lets P0s ship — the class FR-017 fixed for the affected-run gate, reappearing in the one branch the guard skipped.
findings.fix: The blanket early return is deleted (the body returns [] naturally when no branch matches) and vitest `related` now walks the module graph from the changed file, reaching the parent's spec. runAffectedTests reports why the plan is empty, with withoutSpecs.length load-bearing in the "nothing" test: the unexported case says "covered through a parent's spec … add unit-browser to run vitest `related`", the genuinely-empty case (withoutSpecs: []) keeps its old wording; ran:0, green:true retained as an honest "nothing ran". tests/runPlan.test.ts — unexported-only change under unit-browser plans ["unit"] with the exact related command (red with the early return restored); tests/runTests.test.ts — the new reason names "unexported", the withoutSpecs:[] case keeps "nothing affected".

findings.title: useRef was modelled as its init argument, not the ref object
findings.claim: makeEnv folded useRef(null) into null in the render env, so a condition that reads the ref identifier itself (ref ? A : B) resolved the wrong branch — the real ref is always a truthy { current } object. The misbranching is the visible face; the deeper error is that ref.current was reachable as the init arg, a value React does not guarantee (it can be reassigned before the JSX runs).
findings.spirit: An env that models a hook by its first argument rather than its runtime shape picks a branch the component never takes.
findings.fix: A useRef binding resolves to an opaque truthy {}; ref.current evaluates to unknown, never to the init arg — deliberate under-modelling in the safe direction (unknown rather than wrong). tests/renderPath.test.ts gains a makeEnv describe: !ref is false, ref.current is unknown, useState bindings keep their values. Red before, green after. v2 — tracing `ref.current = X` assignments before the JSX — is recorded as B-28.

findings.title: A path parameter before an inline query shipped a dangling ?tab= in the load target
findings.claim: pathOnly's truncation cut the template at the last hole, so /things/${id}?tab=${tab} kept the interpolated query and shipped a dangling `?tab=` — a URL the app never requests. The base path is the load target: a query's values come from runtime state the pipe cannot carry, literal query or interpolated one.
findings.spirit: A load pipe that measures a URL the app never sends is a measurement of nothing.
findings.fix: The template is cut at the first `?` on every path through pathOnly. tests/loadExpo.test.ts — a screen → getThing(id, tab) → apiFetch(`/things/${id}?tab=${tab}`) harvests /things/:id with holes ["id"]; the dangling form reddens without the fix.

findings.title: vitest's value-taking --project was misread as a path filter
findings.claim: selectsAllTests treated --project's argument as a test-path filter: `vitest --project unit` counted the project name as a scope, so a script whose own flags collide with the project name escaped the "you narrowed the run" warning — the operator believes the whole suite ran.
findings.spirit: The warning exists so an operator can tell "whole suite" from "narrowed run"; a flag the scanner cannot read is a warning the operator never sees.
findings.fix: --project joins VALUE_FLAGS (it chooses WHICH project runs, not which tests — `vitest --project unit` still globs that project's whole suite). tests/core.test.ts — --project NAME is flagged, =NAME stays flagged, a real path stays scoped.

findings.title: A "use server" directive behind a long header was missed, and the module misclassified
findings.claim: readPrologueDirective sliced the first 4096 bytes, so a "use server" behind a longer license banner was missed and the module misclassified as client — which then failed to stub the server action in the browser bundle. The read runs once per IMPORTED module in a sweep, so the bound is a perf choice, not a correctness ceiling.
findings.spirit: A classifier that stops reading before the code starts misclassifies whatever the file's author put in the header — and the miss is invisible to everything downstream.
findings.note: The principled fix is to scan to the first token, not to a bigger constant; the constant was raised instead because the read is per-imported-module and 64KB covers any realistic banner. Recorded as B-27.
findings.fix: The bound is raised to 65536 and the docblock names the remaining miss of the bound instead of hiding it. tests/serverActions.test.ts — "use server" behind a ~9KB header is detected; red against the 4096 slice.

findings.title: A browser spec whose component leaves the host is never removed — it fails every run with "unknown component"
findings.claim: Browser specs are emitted only for components that mount standalone (renderMode client). The writer rewrites them every run ONLY while the component STAYS in that set; the in-outDir files' provenance was 'rewritten every run, so no stamp needed'. When a component leaves the mountable set — a new guard the analyser cannot decide, a render-mode change, a deleted file — its spec is simply no longer rendered, and it sits in browser/ forever. The perf-harness registry (regenerated every run) no longer carries the component, so every mount throws 'unknown component' and the spec is red on every run. This is not a user edit gone stale: it is the tool's own regeneration that made the suite red, and no flag or re-run can recover it — the writer has no notion of 'this file should no longer exist'.
findings.spirit: A writer that can create a file but never retire it hands the user a suite that rots: each regeneration silently adds one more spec that references a component the host can no longer mount. 'Identified by being rewritten every run' is only true while the component stays mountable — the exact moment it stops is the moment the assumption breaks.
findings.foundBy: 2026-09 dogfood of the self-review fixes — the apps/web browser plane went red with 6 failures across 4 specs (JobControls, DashboardSidebar, ForgotPasswordForm, ResetPasswordForm), all 'unknown component'. All four had already left the mountable set on main ('Not in this host (72)'), so the red predates the round — the dogfood's full-plane run is what surfaced it.
findings.note: Pre-existing on main, not a regression from this round: the same four specs fail identically at the merge base. The dogfood's value is that it runs the browser plane, which the last several two-task regenerations never did.
findings.fix: Browser specs now carry the same provenance stamp as the colocated specs (the first line hashes the body below it). After the write loop, a sweep lists browser/*.spec.ts not in the run's rendered set and classifies each: an UNTOUCHED stamp is pure tool output for a component the host no longer carries, so it is removed and reported; a mismatched stamp is hand work (kept, reported); no stamp at all is unprovable (kept, reported — this is what protects pre-stamp suites and any spec a user wrote by hand in that directory). The task summary reports both buckets by name, capped like the other kept-listings. --changed narrows the run, never the generation, so the rendered set is always the full one and the sweep is safe under it. Five writer tests, red before / green after: stamp present, removed-when-unrendered, hand-edited-kept, stampless-kept, still-rendered-untouched. Verified end to end on the dogfood app: the 4 stale specs are stampless (pre-stamp), so the sweep keeps and names them in the summary instead of guessing; the owner deletes the four by hand (git history shows none was ever touched after generation), and the browser plane is re-run to prove the red was the staleness and nothing else.

designTensions: perf-static counts a shared leaf once per root that reaches it, so a component imported by many pages multiplies its findings. This is DOCUMENTED INTENDED (the website's triage-findings states it: a shared leaf is reported once per root that reaches it) — the finding belongs to every page that ships it, and the alternative (dedupe to one) hides the multiplicity the triage reader is paying for. Recorded, not changed; left as-is on the record so a future reviewer does not re-derive it as a bug.
deferred: B-27 — prologue-directive principled follow-up (FR-060): scan to the first token (past leading comments/whitespace) instead of a fixed byte bound; the bound is per-imported-module and the cost is bounded

B-28 — useRef v2 (FR-057): trace `ref.current = X` assignments before the JSX so the read evaluates to X; today the deliberate under-modelling returns unknown (safe direction), so this is a coverage gain, not a bug fix
